examples.title: SERGIK x Breauxx - You Can't 1
examples.description: Groove class Funky House / Deep n Funky from measured usage, not from a crate name. Kick is used as a steady four-on-the-floor pulse. Snare is used in a syncopated/dembow cadence. Hats are used as an eighth-note ride that keeps house/tech time. Bass is used off the kick (funky/syncopated), which in a house pocket makes funky house; with sparse hats and sub it can still be reggae/bass. Hats/cymbals are used as a ride over 4/4, so the low-end label is a house/disco sub, not a trap 808 by itself. House is disco's afterlife after the 1979 'Disco Sucks' backlash and the warehouse continuum in Chicago (Knuckles at the Warehouse) and New York (Levan at the Garage). Funky / disco house keeps the offbeat hi-hat and syncopated bass of disco rather than techno's kick-locked ostinato. Nu-disco and French house later re-sampled that language with compression and filters. The science of the style is groove: kick as heartbeat, hats as lift, bass as conversation with the kick. This file's clock is 123 BPM (full-time; 123 BPM). Kick is used as four-on-the-floor; snare as dembow-or-syncopated-snare; hats as eighths. Witek et al. showed moderate syncopation maximizes groove pleasure; too little feels stiff, too much feels broken. Offbeat hats and bass-off-the-kick are the house/disco case of that curve. Sensorimotor synchronization (Large & Snyder; Repp) explains why a stable pulse recruits movement. Club musics around 118–128 BPM sit near preferred tapping rates and walking cadence, which is why four-on-the-floor feels bodily rather than merely metric. Energy below ~60 Hz is felt as vibration (vestibular/tactile) as well as heard. Sound-system culture (Jamaica, UK) and 808 music exploit that channel. A spectral 'sub' label is not automatically trap; house and disco also sit on sub. House floors were historically Black, Latino, and queer sanctuary spaces. The offbeat hat is a social cue — it invites the body to fill the space between kicks. Cross-cultural traffic includes disco strings, gospel piano, Afro-Cuban percussion, and later UK garage shuffle. Related traditions on the map (not extra labels for this file): Chicago House, Disco, Boogie, Nu-Disco, French House, UK Garage, Soulful House, Deep House. Predictable 4/4 plus moderate syncopation supports trance-like motor coupling without the dissociative density of 16th-hat trance. Warm minor/major soul harmony plus swing reads as affiliation and play rather than aggression. Listeners often report 'lift' on the offbeat hat — a small prediction error that resolves every beat. Named center A minor. In many Western listeners, minor collections trend toward lower valence (Juslin/Gabrielsson-type findings) — a tendency, not a universal. Rhythm and bass weight can override that coloring. Estimated arousal 8/10 and dance affordance 9/10 from spectrum, pulse, and hat usage — heuristic, not a lab score.
